comments.note: A03 — SQL Injection (MITIGATED): All SQL in DapperMovieCatalogRepository uses hardcoded constant strings or named Dapper parameters (@Hash, @Filename). MovieListSql, BatchTagSql, and BatchBookmarkDescriptionSql are parameterless constants. MovieExistsAsync, InsertMovieAsync, FilenameExistsAsync, and AddFilenameAsync all pass external values via anonymous-object parameterization. No user-input concatenation present anywhere. No SQL injection surface.

A04 — Insecure Design (INFO): GetMovieListAsync line 311 uses File.Exists(_appPaths.CoverImagePath(item.Hash)) where Hash originates from the database. If a hash value were to contain path traversal characters (e.g. '../../'), CoverImagePath could resolve outside the expected covers directory. In practice hashes are generated by the library scanner (not raw user input) and File.Exists is read-only — no write, execute, or data-exposure risk. Low theoretical concern; no remediation required for a desktop app.

summary: Reviewed 1 file: DapperMovieCatalogRepository.cs. No blocking issues. All 5 ACs met. SQL changes are well-designed: COUNT(DISTINCT mb.bookmark_id) prevents join inflation, MAX aggregate for HasRatedBookmarks correctly identifies movies with any rated bookmark, BatchBookmarkDescriptionSql uses a separate round-trip to avoid the MariaDB GROUP_CONCAT length cap (well-documented rationale). Enrichment pass follows the established ConvertAll/with{} pattern for in-memory enrichment. Minor: step numbering (2.5) is unconventional but non-blocking.

comments.note: COUNT(DISTINCT mb.bookmark_id) is the correct defensive formulation for BookmarkCount. Without DISTINCT, a multi-join SQL query (movies joined to multiple tables) would inflate the count by the Cartesian product of other joined rows. The Developer correctly anticipated this and used DISTINCT throughout (BookmarkCount, HasBookmarks, StoredTagCount, ThumbnailCount).

HasRatedBookmarks uses MAX(CASE WHEN mb.rating > 0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) within the GROUP BY aggregate. This correctly returns 1 if ANY bookmark for a movie has rating > 0, and 0 if all bookmarks have rating = 0 or no bookmarks exist (LEFT JOIN null rows produce 0 from the CASE). Semantics are correct for the AC.

BatchBookmarkDescriptionSql design rationale (separate round-trip to avoid GROUP_CONCAT length cap) is clearly documented in the class-level comment. This is a well-reasoned architectural decision: GROUP_CONCAT has a configurable but often-default 1024-byte limit that would silently truncate results for movies with many bookmarks. The per-row fetch pattern is correct.

Step 2.5 comment numbering in GetMovieListAsync is unconventional — inserting a new query step as '2.5' reads awkwardly. Low priority: in a future cleanup pass, steps 2.5 through 7 could be renumbered to 3–8 for sequential clarity.

[documentation-forward] api-surface.md should document the new batch query pattern in DapperMovieCatalogRepository: three round-trips (MovieListSql, BatchTagSql, BatchBookmarkDescriptionSql) followed by two in-memory enrichment passes and a cover-image pass.
